summary: Following the cutover can lose data: the read-only fence is a session default a client can turn off, and the logical path switches writers without copying large objects or checking them in validation. Rollback timing and backup identity, Cloud SQL internal databases, and several DMS and catalog rules will also send a team to the wrong action, so this SOP needs a rework before use.

findings.claim: The production fence is ALTER DATABASE ... SET default_transaction_read_only = on, then the rollback section tells the approver that nothing was written after the fence. That setting is user-settable, so a direct client can turn it off and commit during validation, and a rollback to the pre-upgrade backup drops those commits.
findings.evidence: SOP: "Set `ALTER DATABASE <db> SET default_transaction_read_only = on` for each app database" and "Nothing was written after the fence, and the smoke tests were read-only, so no data is lost. This holds only if the fence held (Inferred)." Could not fetch https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/runtime-config-client.html. default_transaction_read_only is a user-context GUC: a session, or a connection string options=-c default_transaction_read_only=off, can turn it off and commit.
findings.suggested_fix: Fence by revoking CONNECT from every application role, terminating leftover backends, and confirming pg_stat_activity has no session that can write. Tell the approver that any commit after the backup is data the rollback will drop.

findings.claim: On the logical path, large objects and unlogged tables are dropped at the switch, and neither the ordered cutover nor validate.sql checks them. An in-place upgrade also fails above 10 million large objects, so a database that actually stores large objects has no complete path in this SOP. G3.1 can still pass on table row counts.
findings.evidence: SOP: "Unlogged tables and large objects don't replicate [S-13]." Cutover then says "switch connection strings" with no copy step. B1-09 validation includes "row-count samples". S-13 quotes: "UNLOGGED and TEMPORARY tables aren't and can't be replicated" and "Large Object data type". S-01 quote: "more than 10 million large objects, then the upgrade fails". Reading guide: "any found must be migrated separately or waived by their owner." Live pages were not re-fetched; these are the stored quotes.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a gate that each large object and each unlogged table is copied, dropped with the owner's waiver, or moved with a named tool, and compare pg_largeobject_metadata counts in validate.sql before clients switch.

findings.claim: G2.1 lets the in-window work use 75% of the window, and the rollback decision is the window end minus 1.25 times the rollback duration. Those two rules can both pass when a no-go can no longer finish inside the window. The rehearsal stops the window clock before it times the rollback, so the 75% figure never includes it.
findings.evidence: G2.1: "finish the in-window steps within 75% of the window". Step 13 stops the window clock; step 14 then says "The latest rollback decision time is the window's end minus 1.25 times this duration." A 4 hour window passes G2.1 at 3 hours of upgrade work, while a 1 hour rollback requires the decision 1.25 hours before the end.
findings.suggested_fix: Make G2.1 require that rehearsed in-window time plus 1.25 times rehearsed rollback time fits in the window, and fail the gate when the decision time falls before the upgrade, analyze, and validation have finished.

findings.claim: Cloud SQL keeps two upgrade backups, and the rollback says to restore the pre-upgrade backup without recording its id when the operation starts. After a successful upgrade the later backup is the post-upgrade copy, and restoring that one cannot return the instance to the source version.
findings.evidence: S-01 quotes: "Cloud SQL automatically makes two on-demand backups, called upgrade backups" and "which is made immediately before starting the upgrade". SOP: "Restore the pre-upgrade backup to it [S-01]" and step 7 only "Record the operation ID". Live page not re-fetched; the two-backup wording is the stored quote.
findings.suggested_fix: When the upgrade operation is submitted, record the backup id taken immediately before it, and make the rollback command name that id. Say how the console labels the earlier of the two upgrade backups.

findings.claim: The cutover checkpoint orders a rollback at the decision time, including when replicas were upgraded with the primary, which the same checkpoint says cannot be cancelled. The rehearsed rollback also starts at restore, while this line says a restore waits until cancel has finished, so the 1.25 factor omits cancel time. That restore-after-cancel rule is stated as fact with no source and no Unverified label.
findings.evidence: SOP: "roll back unless the upgrade has finished. ... Cloud SQL can cancel only during the main upgrade phase, and not when replicas are included [S-01]. A restore starts only after the operation is cancelled or has ended." Step 2: upgrading replicas with the primary "rules out cancelling [S-01]". S-01 quotes: "You can only cancel during the main upgrade phase" and "you can't cancel the major version upgrade".
findings.suggested_fix: If replicas are included, state that the upgrade must run to completion before a restore can start, and put that wait in the rehearsed rollback time. Otherwise require the decision record to keep replicas out of the upgrade so cancel stays available. Mark the restore-after-cancel rule Unverified until the provider confirms it.

findings.claim: Every section 6c row is a production blocker that G1.1 must clear on a kit rerun. The same SOP excludes Cloud SQL's cloudsqladmin from the per-database loop because it is provider-internal, and the kit flags every non-template0 database that rejects connections. A normal Cloud SQL instance therefore keeps a 6c row that the customer cannot fix, so G1.1 cannot close on a clean rerun.
findings.evidence: SOP: "6c (databases pg_upgrade can't connect to) ... blocks pg_upgrade 18" and G1.1 requires every G0.4 blocker "fixed in production" with a rerun of "6a to 6g". Step 3: "Provider-internal ones, such as Cloud SQL's `cloudsqladmin`, don't" get their own file. Kit: "(datname <> 'template0' AND (NOT datallowconn OR datconnlimit = -2))". S-22 quote: "pg_database.datallowconn must be true and pg_database.datconnlimit". The reading guide says to ask the provider before changing a provider-managed database; the SOP gate does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude provider-internal databases from the 6c blocker rule, or add an explicit provider question whose answer closes that row. Keep a customer database with datallowconn false or datconnlimit -2 as a real blocker.

findings.claim: Section 6 is the outline for DMS, pglogical, and pgcopydb, but the sequence and backup rules it requires are DMS limitations. A pglogical or pgcopydb cutover that waits for DMS-style promotion, or that assumes PITR was suspended and must be turned back on, follows the wrong recovery procedure.
findings.evidence: SOP intro: "the logical path (DMS, pglogical or pgcopydb)". Then: "Sequences sync only at promotion [S-13]" and "Automated backups and point-in-time recovery are suspended on the destination during continuous replication [S-13]. Turn them back on after promotion, before reopening." S-13 title is "Database Migration Service: Known limitations (PostgreSQL)". Quotes: "Sequence values are synchronized during the final promotion step" and "Automated backups and point-in-time recovery (PITR) are suspended during continuous replication".
findings.suggested_fix: Mark the PITR suspension and promotion-time sequence sync as DMS-only. For pglogical and pgcopydb, require a tool-specific sequence catch-up check before writes reopen, and a separate check that destination backups stayed on.

findings.claim: The SOP says a standard DMS migration does not carry UPDATEs or DELETEs for tables without a primary key. The same cited source says those operations replicate when replica identity is INDEX or FULL, so a team can add primary keys under a rewrite lock, or accept lost updates, on a path the source already allows.
findings.evidence: SOP: "A standard DMS migration carries INSERTs on tables without a primary key, but not UPDATEs or DELETEs [S-13]." S-13 stored quote: "primary keys aren't required to replicate UPDATE and DELETE operations if you set the replica identity to INDEX or FULL". The reading guide states that exception; section 6 does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Quote the replica-identity exception next to the keyless-table rule, and make the decision record choose primary keys, replica identity INDEX or FULL, or an owner waiver that updates will be dropped.

findings.claim: When stats coverage held, the SOP still analyzes every partitioned parent that has no pg_stats row. In PostgreSQL 18, ANALYZE on a parent processes inheritance children unless ONLY is used, so this path re-analyzes partitions that already have stats and can consume the window the selective analyze was meant to protect.
findings.evidence: The coverage-held query selects "c.relkind IN ('r', 'm', 'p')" and "(c.relkind = 'p' OR pg_relation_size(c.oid) > 0)" with no ONLY. The same step says "In 18, VACUUM and ANALYZE also process inheritance children [S-17]." S-17 quote: "Change VACUUM and ANALYZE to process the inheritance children of a parent". Appendix A says "unless ONLY".
findings.suggested_fix: Analyze partitions and ordinary tables individually, and use ANALYZE ONLY for parents. Time that statement list in the rehearsal and keep it inside the G2.1 budget.

findings.claim: G1.4 resets every password-login role on the source version before the window, and the task list has no step to publish the new secret and restart clients first. Those passwords stop working at the moment of the reset, which can lock applications out well before cutover.
findings.evidence: G1.4: "Every password-login role has had its password reset under `scram-sha-256`, or has its owner's waiver". B1-04: "reset every password-login role's password under SCRAM, and check that each driver supports SCRAM". The rotation log records "each role and date", with no client-cutover step.
findings.suggested_fix: Order the work as driver confirmation, secret rollout, client restart, then the password reset. Allow a role that is already SCRAM to be waived once the provider or a superuser-equivalent check shows it is not MD5.

findings.claim: B1-02 tells the agent to add the missing NOT NULL constraints from section 6d. The reading guide says to stop when the child column contains nulls and get a data decision from the owner. An agent migration that deletes or rewrites those nulls to force SET NOT NULL changes production data.
findings.evidence: B1-02: "add the missing NOT NULLs from 6d". Reading guide section 6d: "Count the nulls in the child column first. If there are none, the DBA adds `SET NOT NULL` on the child. If there are any, stop, because the data needs a decision from its owner first."
findings.suggested_fix: Put the null count in the B1-02 task. Allow the migration only when the count is zero; otherwise open an owner decision and keep the row blocked.

findings.claim: G0.4 treats an empty section 6a as proof that no reg* type blocks pg_upgrade 18. The kit's type list omits regrole, so a regrole column, or a domain or array over it, clears the gate and fails in pg_upgrade.
findings.evidence: SOP: "6a (reg* types, `aclitem`, system composite types) ... blocks pg_upgrade 18. All four are Verified in pg_upgrade's own checks [S-22]." Kit base names: regcollation, regconfig, regdictionary, regnamespace, regoper, regoperator, regproc, regprocedure. Could not fetch https://raw.githubusercontent.com/postgres/postgres/REL_18_STABLE/src/bin/pg_upgrade/check.c. S-22's stored quotes include "regcollation" and do not list every typname; the community check also includes regrole.
findings.suggested_fix: Add regrole to the section 6a base list, including domains, arrays, and composites built on it, and re-check the list against check.c before calling 6a complete.

findings.claim: B1-13 installs the pending minor, including 14.24, on production before rehearsals, while B1-14 allows the btree_gist float and ltree reindex to wait for a cutover runbook step. Until that reindex, those indexes still use the old NaN ordering. The same reindex is also required on a jump from an earlier 14 minor straight to 18, because pg_upgrade copies the index.
findings.evidence: B1-14: "`btree_gist` float opclasses and `ltree` after 14.24 [S-21]" and "Each becomes a fix task or a timed runbook step." B1-13: "Apply any pending minor update before the rehearsal". S-21 quotes: "you may need to reindex indexes made with those extensions" and "fix NaN handling in the float4 and float8 opclasses".
findings.suggested_fix: Reindex the affected btree_gist and ltree indexes immediately after the minor that contains the NaN fix, and again after any major upgrade that lands on binaries with that fix. Do not leave the reindex until cutover.

findings.claim: The reindex inventory covers btree_gist, ltree, non-libc full-text and pg_trgm indexes, and nondeterministic primary and foreign keys. It does not require a reindex when the operating system's collation library changed, so ordinary text indexes can return wrong rows after a Cloud SQL major upgrade moves the instance to a new image.
findings.evidence: B1-14 lists "`btree_gist` float opclasses and `ltree`", "full-text search and `pg_trgm` indexes on clusters whose default collation provider isn't libc [S-17]", and "primary and foreign key pairs on nondeterministic collations". Could not fetch https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/pgupgrade.html. S-14's stored quotes cover statistics transfer and "--swap" only.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a provider question and a rehearsal check for collation-library version mismatch, and reindex every index that depends on a changed collation before writers reopen.

findings.claim: In-place rollback repoints the pooler and apps, while the logical cutover walks Block 0's consumer rows. A consumer whose recorded path is the primary keeps writing to the upgraded instance after the pooler moves to the recovery instance.
findings.evidence: Rollback: "Repoint the pooler and apps." Logical cutover: "switch connection strings, using Block 0's consumer rows as the switch list." G0.1 evidence is a connection path of "primary, replica or pooler" per consumer.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the in-place rollback repoint every G0.1 consumer row, including direct primary connections, and confirm the census shows no sessions left on the upgraded instance before the recovery instance is opened for writes.

findings.claim: The SOP reads as a general major-version procedure, while the decision gate records PostgreSQL 14 support dates and the precheck command targets POSTGRES_18. A team on another source or target will sign the wrong support dates and run the wrong provider precheck.
findings.evidence: G0.6: "the source version's support dates (for 14: community updates end in November 2026 [S-21], and Cloud SQL extended support starts 2027-02-01 [S-02])". B0-04: "--target-database-version=POSTGRES_18". precheck.sql header: "Written for Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL 14 -> 18." The title is "Postgres major version upgrade: SOP".
findings.suggested_fix: State on the first page that this version of the SOP is Cloud SQL PostgreSQL 14 to 18. Make the source and target parameters, and look up support dates for the source that Block 0 actually found.

findings.claim: The SOP says sources were rechecked live on 2026-11-04, and it cites S-34, S-35, S-36, and S-37 as settled facts for query plans, the maintenance freeze, password hashes, and wraparound. Those four rows have no verification status and do not appear in sources.md, so the claims never say how they get settled.
findings.evidence: SOP: "Sources were rechecked live on that date ([sources.md](sources.md))." sources.md: "Treat claims that cite it as Unverified until someone rechecks." sources.json S-34 through S-37 contain quotes and omit status, lastChecked, and verified. They are absent from the sources.md table. The SOP uses them at the queryid sentence [S-34], the 90-day deny period [S-35], pg_authid [S-36], and wraparound [S-37].
findings.suggested_fix: Re-run the quote check for S-34 through S-37 and list them in sources.md. Until that passes, mark each SOP sentence that cites them Unverified and name the rehearsal or provider answer that closes it.

findings.claim: The SOP says a CHECK-constraint function that relies on search_path can fail the upgrade, and tells the team to fix every section 6g row. Section 6g never selects CHECK constraints, so this class is outside the gate evidence. The stored S-18 quote describes maintenance operations and does not mention CHECK constraints.
findings.evidence: SOP: "a function used in an index, materialized view, generated column or CHECK constraint that relies on `search_path` can fail." Kit 6g covers index dependencies, generated columns, and materialized views, and does not query pg_constraint. S-18 quote: "Change functions to use a safe search_path during maintenance operations". Could not re-fetch the release notes.
findings.suggested_fix: Either extend section 6g to CHECK constraints and cite the note that covers them, or remove CHECK constraints from the blocker paragraph so G0.4 matches the kit.

findings.claim: The logical outline says materialized views arrive empty and need REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, but the ordered cutover validates and switches connection strings with no refresh. Clients can read empty materialized views as soon as they switch.
findings.evidence: SOP: "Materialized views arrive empty and need `REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW` [S-13]." Cutover: "promote, and validate. Then switch connection strings". S-13 quote: "doesn't migrate data from materialized views, just the view schema".
findings.suggested_fix: Put REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW in the cutover sequence before the switch, and add a non-empty check for each materialized view to validate.sql.

findings.claim: The extension-catalog sentence cites S-10 as fact. sources.md marks S-10 changed on 2026-11-04 and says claims that cite a changed source stay Unverified until someone rechecks. The SOP does not say how this sentence gets settled.
findings.evidence: SOP: "Cloud SQL maintenance installs new extension binaries but doesn't update an extension's catalog version [S-10]." sources.md row S-10 status: "changed 2026-11-04", and the header says "Treat claims that cite it as Unverified until someone rechecks."
findings.suggested_fix: Mark the S-10 sentence Unverified until the quote check is green again, and confirm ALTER EXTENSION ... UPDATE against the current extensions page before Block 1 relies on it.

findings.claim: G2.4 can be closed on "no open plan regressions", and the analyze branch turns on "near zero" stats coverage. Neither phrase has a threshold, a comparison rule, or a required artifact, so two reviewers can close the gates on different evidence.
findings.evidence: G2.4: "within 2x of its source-version time, with no open plan regressions". Step 9: "If coverage dropped to near zero: run `vacuumdb --all --analyze-in-stages` inside the window." The 2x timing rule is measurable; "plan regressions" and "near zero" are not defined.
findings.suggested_fix: Define a plan regression as a named change in node type or a row-estimate ratio, recorded in the timing sheet. Define the coverage drop as a numeric fraction of tables_with_stats over readable_nonempty_tables.
